I like to have a mission statement before I do anything, because without a stated goal, you don't know if the action you're taking is effective. We're not going to have rules "just because" - we'll have rules for a specific purpose. Here's my mission: since there are already lots of places on the internet for general discussion and for airing grievances (and hell, you can start your own blog for that too), and since there aren't very many people here on voat anyway, I want this place to have fewer posts, but higher quality posts.

So here's what I'm thinking in terms of rules, and I welcome feedback.

(1) No generalized gendered slurs

What?? Seriously??

Yeah. I'll join you on any other MGTOW forum and we can shoot the shit and complain about any group in general. "Kids today are little shits" - posts like that. But here, in this one little corner of the internet, that'll be against the rules.

"Generalized" means "addressing the entire group." An example might be, "men are dicks." That's generalized. By contrast, when discussing a specific individual, feel free apply whatever label you think you can support. "PZ Myers is an dick" is a statement that is both allowed and factually correct.

"Gendered-slur" means "an insult that makes reference to sex or gender." I used "dick" above as an example. "Men are assholes" on the other hand is generalizing but not using a gendered slur.

See, the problem that I'm trying to solve here is that this specific language both decreases the signal-to-noise ratio (that is, it invites low-effort carbon copy posts that just complain - and like I said, I'll join you on any other forum to do that) and it also distracts from whatever point you thought you were making. People are just going to reply that not all women are like that, or whatever. It's just a waste of time.

If you're thinking to yourself, "I am totally unable to express myself without making use of generalized gendered slurs" then you're probably not articulate enough to post here.

(2) When disagreeing with the MGTOW POV, no sarcasm

What?? Seriously??

Yeah. See, the problem with sarcasm is that I have to unpack it before I can respond to you. That creates an additional and unnecessary level of ambiguity. If you want to disagree with me or MGTOW, then it's your job to communicate your disagreement successfully. If you aren't willing or able to do that (and most trolls wont be able to do it) then fuck off.

If you're thinking to yourself, "I am totally unable to express my objection to MGTOW without snark and sarcasm" then you're probably not actually as clever as you like to believe.

Note that this rule only applies to disagreement. As above, it's designed to maintain the signal-to-noise ratio by keeping out trolls, while still welcoming intelligent criticism.

First original guitar ive wrote pointers?,

Just keep practicing. I can tell what you're trying to do but your technique just isn't quite good enough to pull it off yet.

The best thing you could do I think would be to play this over a drum beat/loop of some sort. At the very least play it to a metronome click and record that.

Either your guitar is out of tune or the intonation is really bad. A quick guitar setup will fix that for you. You'll also just want to practice your bends to make sure you're actually bending strings up to pitch. Again, kinda of a beginner-intermediate guitar thing that you're just going to have to spend time practicing to develop.

Everyone's ear works differently but to me it's not really a 'song' until you have a melody. The easiest way to work on that would be to either sing (it's never too late to practice singing if you've never done it before and totally suck at it) or just record this guitar part and then record a second guitar part over it doing a really simple lead line to function as the 'vocal melody'.

Spending a little bit of time learning the major/minor scale and some basic chord progressions should also influence your writing in a positive way, too. I ii iii IV V vi vii

Audacity is a great free audio recording program you can use to accomplish all of those things. Once you know what tempo the song is you can use the "Generate Click Track" function to create a metronome beep that you then listen to as you're playing to keep things consistent and in time.

After you record one layer, just create a new track and record a second one to accompany it. You can do the same to add a bass line if you have a bass guitar.

The technology is so easy these days and makes songwriting so much easier it's absolutely worth the time to learn how to use it.

It sounds like the guitar is a little out of tune. If it seems to be tuned up correctly with your tuner, you might want to get it closer by checking your intonation. The second thing I noticed is your rhythm--it's not rock solid yet. Two solutions for this: Keep your right hand strumming even on the rests so that when it needs to hit the strings it's on beat, like this. Lasty, practice your song along with a metronome, I can't stress this enough.
